items.label: Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan)
items.value_label: 48.0, October final (Oct 23), revised up from the 46.3 preliminary
items.say: Still among the lowest readings in the survey's history; the final October figure was revised up to nearly September's level.
items.src: Trading Economics calendar (University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers), Oct 23

items.label: Gasoline, national average (AAA)
items.compare: $3.053 a year ago; $4.295 a week ago; $4.487 a month ago
items.say: Up about 40% in a year, though a cent lower than a week ago and 20 cents below a month ago.

items.label: A Chipotle chicken burrito bowl
items.say: Roughly 15–20% more than four years ago; restaurant prices overall are up 3.4% in the past year (CPI food away from home, August).
items.src: Reuters via ThePricer (May 2026); Food Business News (Oct 2022)

items.label: Prediction markets: Democratic House
items.compare: Senate: about 65% Democratic from the balance-of-power contracts (Democrats win both 63.5¢ on Kalshi and 65.5¢ on Polymarket; Democratic House with Republican Senate 28.5¢ and 26.5¢; Republican House with Democratic Senate under 1¢; Republicans win both 9.3¢ and 7.5¢)
items.say: Markets sit between the polls-only model and the expert raters; the Senate price has drifted down from about 68% a week ago.

items.label: Cook Political Report House ratings
items.compare: Cook's projection (Oct 23): Democrats gain 12-22 seats, 227-237; after 19 more moves toward Democrats on Oct 23: Solid/Likely/Lean D 220, Toss Up 17, Lean/Likely/Solid R 198. Senate (Oct 20): 7 Toss Ups, 6 Republican-held, after South Carolina and Mississippi moved toward Democrats and Minnesota toward Republicans
items.say: Democrats need none of the toss-ups for a majority if the seats leaning their way hold.

items.label: House members not seeking re-election
items.say: More Republicans leaving, including 20 running for other office; retirements have not tracked the swing in past midterms.
